 sanket koul New Delhi, 10 November The Department of Pharma- ceuticals (DoP) has extended the production-linked incen- tive (PLI) scheme to promote domestic manufacturing of medical devices by eight years, until 2035-36. Inviting fresh applications under the extended scheme, DoP said that the roughly ~2,700 crore outlay available under the existing scheme would be utilised for the pur- pose. “Applicants can submit applications through an online portal, which will be operational in the next 10 days,” officials aware of the matter said. They added that several eligibility conditions had been relaxed based on the learnings from the ﬁrst phase of the scheme. While DoP did not provide details, it said on Tuesday that the minimum sales threshold requirement for claiming incentives had been discon- tinued. Officials added that the minimum investment require- ment of ~180 crore had also been reduced to make the scheme more investor-friendly. Similarly, applicants will now be allowed three years to set up manufacturing facilities across four distinct target seg- ments (TS). This marks a departure from the earlier PLI framework, under which com- panies often had a very tight turnaround time — sometimes just one year or until a ﬁxed commercial date — to com- mence production. Under the new framework, the four target segments will include medical consumables, disposables and implants (TS1), and critical components (TS2). TS3 will cover high-end medical devices that are cur- rently at a nascent stage of domestic manufacturing, while TS4 will include high- end medical devices that are presently only assembled in the country. “In TS3 and TS4, priority shall be given to value chain integration so that there is an overall increase in the competitiveness and quality of Made in India devices,” DoP said in a statement. The revised scheme will also introduce a tapering incentive structure, with rates of 5 per cent for TS1, 9 per cent for TS2 and TS3, and 6 per cent for TS4. This marks a change from the earlier ﬂat incentive rate applicable to eligible incre- mental sales made by partici- pants annually. “The incentives now match the difficulty of manufactur- ing. Instead of one ﬂat rate, higher rates go where manu- facturing is hardest and import dependence is deepest,” a Delhi-based medical technol- ogy (medtech) manufacturer told Business Standard. Announced in March 2020, the PLI scheme for medical devices has resulted in produc- tion worth over ~16,000 crore, according to DoP. “The scheme has led to domestic manufac- turing of over 60 high-end devices and components, including X-ray tubes and detectors, 1.5-tesla magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) machines, cath labs and dia- lysers, among others, to date,” the department said. Officials quoted above added that the objective of the revised framework was to pro- mote deeper domestic manu- facturing of medical devices, as well as the production of high- end equipment such as 3T MRI machines, PET-CT scanners, ultrasound consoles and high- throughput IVD analysers, which are currently not manu- factured in the country. Medical device PLI scheme extended by 8 yrs; focus shifts to components
